title.narrative: Fostering a safe and enabling environment for inclusive and sustainable peacebuilding

description.narrative: Overall objectives: a safe and enabling environment for inclusive and sustainable peacebuilding is fostered. Specific objective 1: violence and its effect on civilians, particularly women and children, is reduced and responded to. Specific objective 2: Community Protection Teams are strengthened and entrenched as integral structures in their community. Specific objective 3: communities are better positioned to influence local authorities and state mechanism on civic decision-making processes and peace processes. Specific objective 4: social cohesion is increased within and between communities.

title.narrative: Output 1.1 Violence and its effect on civilians, particularly women and children, is reduced and responded to.

description.narrative: Activity 1.1.1: Conduct strategic patrolling and protective presence for civilians in conflict locations. Where possible, NP will conduct these patrols jointly with WPTs and YPTs.Activity 1.1.2: Provide protective accompaniments & referrals for GBV survivors, children and other civilians facing immediate threats to life, and monitor and report on grave violations against children.Activity 1.1.3: Supporting the establishment, strengthening, and improved utilization of child protection and SGBV referral pathways. Activity 1.1.4: Provision of safe spaces, recreational activities, life-skills trainings and community-based support for children.

title.narrative: Output 3.2: Marginalized social groups are linked to local, state and national leadership and Humanitarian, Development and Peacebuilding (HDP) partner organizations, judiciaries and other persons in power.

description.narrative: Activity 3.2.1: Marginalized groups, including youth, women and persons with disabilities are linked to local and state leadership, including traditional leaders, government officials and judiciaries.Activity 3.2.2: Community members, in particular women and youth, are linked to humanitarian partners working across the HDP nexus to gain more agency and ownership over humanitarian aid provided in their communities.

title.narrative: Output 4.1 Communities have increased knowledge of social cohesion.

description.narrative: Activity 4.1.1: Based on in-depth context analyses, educational and training materials on social cohesion are developed and adapted for the targeted populations. Activity 4.1.2: Trainings are provided on social cohesion.Activity 4.1.3: Awareness-raising and trainings around formal and customary justice mechanisms to support the establishment of inclusive justice mechanisms as needed and build confidence in existing justice and law enforcement mechanisms, including the Women and Gender Desk of local Police Departments.

title.narrative: Output 4.2 Communities have increased opportunities for fostering trust between themselves and with ‘other’ communities.

description.narrative: Activity 4.2.1: Facilitate community dialogues, activities and safe spaces for community members and leaders to share and discuss critical protection concerns and root problems, assess and map out issues that hamper social cohesion, and support trust and relationship building in a safe space.Activity 4.2.2: Facilitate intra- and intercommunal dialogues to prevent, mitigate and respond to the escalation of violence, or to increase social cohesion between and within communities.Activity 4.2.3: Conduct regional, state and county level conferences and meetings that create space for women and youth, separately and jointly, to identify and strategize avenues for increased participation and influence in the peace and decision-making processes at the state and sub-national levels.Activity 4.2.4: Facilitate joint activities between CPTs and other community groups, including religious leaders and local peace councils.

title.narrative: Output 1.2: Communities are equipped to more effectively prevent violence.

description.narrative: •Activity 1.2.1: Conflict analysis is collaboratively developed through community protection meetings.•Activity 1.2.2: Enhance communities’ knowledge on Small Arms Light Weapons (SALW), culminating in Weapon Free Zones (WFZs) when appropriate.•Activity 1.2.3: Provision of UCP trainings, including trainings on gender-equality, child protection and GBV prevention and response, to community members, CPTs, community leadership, local authorities, judiciaries and armed actors.•Activity 1.2.4: Communities are trained on Early Warning Early Response and develop EWER action plans through collaborative workshops.

title.narrative: Output 1.3 The centrality of protection is increasingly integrated into humanitarian responses amongst partner organizations, community security duty bearers, local CSOs, and NNGOs

description.narrative: •Activity 1.3.1 Coordination meetings with international and national partner organizations to improve the coordination amongst humanitarian, development and protection interventions.•Activity 1.3.2: Provide protection technical advice and planning/implementation support for agencies conducting material aid and food distributions on a needs-basis.

title.narrative: Output 2.1: Community Protection Teams are trained and/or mentored on addressing protection concerns, peacebuilding, and leadership

description.narrative: •Activity 2.1.1: Facilitate the establishment, strengthening and operationalization of WPTs, YPTs, Gender Champion groups and other community-based protection structures, including mentorship sessions to build confidence and leadership skills.•Activity 2.1.2: Provide trainings of trainers and refresher workshops to CPTs on protection and peacebuilding, including SGBV prevention and response, child protection, negotiation and advocacy, conflict mitigation and response, basic psychological first aid and self-protection, and encouraging them to be focal points within their communities.

title.narrative: Output 2.2: Independent activities by Community Protection Teams are facilitated and supported.

description.narrative: •Activity 2.2.1: Supporting, preparing and facilitating independent activities conducted by Community Protection Teams related to unarmed civilian protection, gender equality, social cohesion and rule of law.•Activity 2.2.2: Mentor and support women and youth-led community peace dialogues, advocacy efforts and the implementation of locally-led protection and peacebuilding strategies at community and state levels.

title.narrative: Output 3.1: Harmful social norms are addressed and challenged to support marginalized social groups, including women, youth and persons with disabilities

description.narrative: •Activity 3.1.1: Gender analysis is conducted in each of the areas of operations and educational strategies to address harmful gender norms, prejudice against youth and other marginalized groups are updated and adapted for the target groups, per field location. •Activity 3.1.2: Conduct community outreach and awareness raising activities on gender equality, nonviolent conflict prevention and response, and adoption of positive and nonviolent masculinities and techniques with all community members including specific activities targeted at key groups (men and boys, adolescents and children).•Activity 3.1.3: Conduct conflict prevention, protection mainstreaming, child protection and SGVB training sessions/workshops with law enforcement, judiciary, traditional and local leadership engaged in ensuring resolution of SGBV cases in the community, including the establishment of Women and Gender Desks with local police departments where necessary
